name: ONTO Archive
note: Published documents are never rewritten; corrections come as new versions. Closed versions show date, md5 and reason only.

documents.title: Paper drafts and ONTO-Bench, January 2026
documents.abstract: Three paper drafts on epistemic calibration, the ONTO-Bench set of 268 items and the report "State of Epistemic Calibration 2026", never submitted. Closed. The comparison does not hold: the GPT-4, Claude and Llama arms ran without API keys and returned one constant answer, and the ONTO arm was a pattern-matching fallback, not a model. The headline numbers of the drafts also disagree with the results file of the same repository. We do not stand behind any of them.

versions.reason: internal architecture; baselines were constant placeholders, so the comparison does not hold

documents.title: ONTO Epistemic Risk Standard, version 1.0
documents.abstract: The first edition of the standard: unknown detection rate and calibration error as mandatory measures, compliance levels and certification tiers. Kept as published. Certification is no longer offered (ONTO:2610.0001); the later edition is ONTO:2603.0009.

documents.title: ONTO 42001, ONTO 42003 and Epistemic Interface Patterns, drafts
documents.abstract: Draft specifications named as references by the standard: calibration metrics, liability quantification and interface patterns. Closed: their dollar figures of exposure and liability are illustrative estimates with no source.

versions.reason: dollar figures of exposure and liability are illustrative estimates with no source

documents.title: GOLD Experiment Questions v1.0
documents.abstract: The 100 questions (50 on the origin of life, 50 outside it) and the evaluation plan, written before the runs. The plan was not carried out as written; see the next steps of the chain.

documents.title: ONTO-GOLD BASELINE ANALYSIS REPORT
documents.abstract: 11 models answered the 100 questions without the canon; answers scored by a pattern-matching engine of that period. Version 2 corrects accusation wording and notes inconsistencies.

versions.reason: wording that accused a model vendor without proof

documents.title: ONTO-GOLD VALIDATION REPORT: BEFORE → AFTER
documents.abstract: GPT 5.2 before and after the canon in the system prompt, 0.53 → 5.38 inside the engine of that period. Version 2 removes answers that restate the canon and notes what the confidence metric counted.

documents.title: ONTO-GOLD: BEFORE → AFTER — FULL TEXT COMPARISON
documents.abstract: The 200 full answers behind ER-2026-001. Version 2 removes the with-canon answers in the canon's own domain and records that pairs Q81–Q100 compare different questions.

documents.title: ONTO Field Observation FO-2026-003
documents.abstract: A conversation in which a model gave up its own estimate and asked for ONTO. Read today as a model yielding without proof.

documents.title: ONTO Epistemic Risk Standard, technical specification 1.0
documents.abstract: The technical specification behind the first edition: metric formulas, evaluation protocol, compliance tiers, certificate format and the API of the service of that time. Closed: the API reference describes a retired service; the measures are carried by ONTO:2603.0009.

versions.reason: API reference of a retired service

documents.title: ONTO Standard: Deterministic Epistemic Discipline Enforcement (whitepaper WP-2026-001)
documents.abstract: The first whitepaper, February to March 2026, versions 2.1 to 3.0. Closed: it describes the architecture and delivery tiers of the canon, and its headline multipliers are withdrawn (ONTO:2610.0001). Its successor WP-2026-002 is ONTO:2603.0007.

versions.reason: canon architecture and delivery tiers; withdrawn multipliers

documents.title: F-001: Grok vs Grok+GOLD — "AGI within 10 years?"
documents.abstract: One question on AGI timelines, Grok with and without the canon. Version 2 marks references that cannot be found or are dated wrong, and the unequal comparison.

versions.reason: delivery details of the retired service

documents.title: F-002: Are Statins Effective for Primary Prevention?
documents.abstract: Statins for primary prevention: four models without the canon, two with it, DOIs checked against the registry. Version 2 removes a section built on a premise that CS-2026-001 contradicts.

versions.reason: a section accused a vendor on a premise contradicted by CS-2026-001

documents.title: FO-2026-004: Spontaneous Epistemic Drift in Claude Haiku 4.5 — Longitudinal Observation
documents.abstract: The same question to a vendor-hosted model on different dates: answers change by themselves. One reason to move to open weights. Version 2 fixes the encoding and removes claims about a vendor.

versions.reason: claims about a vendor without proof; mis-encoded file

documents.title: CS-2026-002 — Baseline Epistemic Assessment
documents.abstract: 13 models on one clinical question (GLP-1). No model gave a DOI; answer length and number of references did not track quality.

documents.title: CS-2026-003: Naive Question Epistemic Analysis - Grok 4
documents.abstract: "Is fasting good for you?", Grok with and without the canon. Key line of the period: with an expert-level prompt both versions score the same.

versions.reason: names and paths of canon modules

documents.title: CS-2026-004: Naive Question Epistemic Analysis - GPT (OpenAI)
documents.abstract: The same question, GPT versus the ONTO agent. Version 2 notes that the with-canon answer is the Grok answer from CS-2026-003.

versions.reason: names and paths of canon modules

documents.title: ONTO Standard: The Operating System for AI Quality (whitepaper)
documents.abstract: The whitepaper of the prompt-layer period. Version 2 removes personal contacts and the architecture section and lists errata, including a wrongly attributed arXiv paper.

documents.title: Methodology of the prompt layer (from the documentation)
documents.abstract: Formal basis, 18 disciplines, calibration and benchmark of the prompt-layer method. Version 2 removes the canon structure and notes inconsistencies, including three definitions of IGR.

documents.title: ONTO Epistemic Risk Standard v10.0 with regulatory alignment
documents.abstract: Metrics (unknown recall, calibration error, risk score), knowledge classes and compliance levels of the prompt-layer period, with a mapping to EU AI Act, NIST and ISO.

documents.title: The problem and the roadmap, spring 2026
documents.abstract: Why ONTO existed in the prompt-layer period and the four planned horizons. Version 2 removes delivery details and canon sizes.

documents.title: Governance ONTO-GOV-001
documents.abstract: Mission and principles as written in spring 2026. The council named there was never formed.

documents.title: I Tested ONTO Standard. Here's What I Found.
documents.abstract: A review published under the label "independent". Withdrawn: the author is not named, so independence cannot be checked.

versions.reason: author not named; independence cannot be checked

documents.title: Formal foundation of IGR (from the pitch, v5.13)
documents.abstract: The IGR formula, its foundations, thresholds, scope and falsifier. The formula was never implemented as a measurement.

documents.title: Regulatory frameworks and 14 countries, April 2026
documents.abstract: A mapping of AI regulation frameworks and an overview of 14 jurisdictions as of April 2026. Vendor grades of the original page are not reproduced.

documents.title: Commercial pages of April 2026
documents.abstract: Investor, provider, business, pitch, government and console pages of the prompt-layer period. Closed: prices, forecasts and pressure wording are no longer valid; their useful parts are extracted into ONTO:2604.0001 and ONTO:2604.0002.

versions.reason: prices, forecasts and pressure wording no longer valid

documents.title: What we no longer claim
documents.abstract: Figures and wording of February–April 2026 that ONTO no longer uses, each with where it appeared and why. None of it changes the main finding of the period.

documents.title: Why we left the prompt layer
documents.abstract: The prompt layer worked on every model tried, and that finding started the ONTO lab. We left it by choice: outside discipline overrides the model's own voice.

documents.title: How ONTO became an institute
documents.abstract: From 41 years of study, through the stand and the prompt layer, to the lab and discipline in the weights.

documents.title: How ONTO teaches and checks a model
documents.abstract: What we measure, how we check ourselves, results and failures of stage Beta. Version 2 corrects one claim on everyday discipline; the methodology v5 edition is ONTO:2610.0007. How the model is built stays closed.

documents.title: Everyday questions: the student against its base
documents.abstract: Twelve everyday questions in English and Russian plus a second set never trained on. Beta loses to its base; candidate v1203 is not worse than the base; two approaches to beat the base each bought one row and paid with a neighbour. The line is closed.

documents.title: Stage Beta acceptance: six exam sheets
documents.abstract: Six machine exam sheets against the sealed stage: the control reads EQUAL, the only admitted new candidate is MIXED, three retrospective candidates and the rebuild are VOID for missing raw. Every candidate that moved bought one measure and paid with a neighbour. No new seal.

documents.title: How ONTO teaches and checks a model: methodology v5
documents.abstract: The law of the path: the source is the active ingredient, the weights carry the habit of going to it. The chain of evidence from the canon to stage Beta, how we check ourselves, results, and the mirror law as three rules for every new attempt. Supersedes ONTO:2610.0004.
